who: two watchmen on a wall or tower

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Anything?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Same as an hour ago. Dark, and more dark.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Keep looking. Dark's where they come from.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Your eyes are shutting, {B}.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: They're resting. My ears are on watch.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Tell your ears the sergeant's coming up the stair.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: There's the light. We lived.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Don't say that till the relief's up the ladder.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: They say {band} burned {hamlet} to the ground.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Then they'll want something bigger next.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Like us. Keep your bow strung.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: See that glow past the Rim?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: That's no hearth fire.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Pray it's the Heart turning over in its sleep, and nothing more.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Watch pay's late again.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: In Reedwatch? Watch pay's a rumour.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Then why are we up here?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Because the Crows don't pay at all.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Wind off the Wall cuts like a knife tonight.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: My grandfather stood this post in worse. Stop your whining.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Can't watch on an empty belly.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Then watch the cookhouse. If it smokes, tell me first.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Beacons are lit on the line.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Every dusk. Nobody knows why anymore.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Old Walter Underhill knows. He just won't say.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: A new one's risen in the March. {calamity}.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Don't say its name on watch.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Why not?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Because it might be listening for it.

who: two woodcutters or servants at a chopping block

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Split it small. The cook won't fight a log.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: The cook would fight a bear.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Aye, and the bear would lose.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Is this the lord's wood or the lodge's?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Deadfall's anybody's. Don't cut anything green.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Woodpile's higher than the wall.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Good. Winter doesn't care how fat the summer was.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: We're burning wood for warmth since there's nothing to cook.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Warmth's something. Keep chopping.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Sawmill takes the good timber. We get the knots.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Knots burn hotter. Brother says it's humility.

who: two poachers in the lord's wood

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Quiet. There's a hind past the beech.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Lord's deer, then.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Lord's deer don't know whose belly they'll fill.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Lantern down. Foresters walk the ride at night now.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Foresters walk where the wine is. We're fine.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: The Half Law says leave half.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: The Half Law never fed my children.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Take the yearling, then. Leave the mothers.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Lodge lost another hunter in the woods.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Wasn't us.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Doesn't matter. They'll hang the first poacher they find.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Old royal park's got the fattest deer in the realm.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Thornback lads have been eating like kings off it.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Bring back the haunch, leave the hide.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Hides get you hanged. Haunches get you thanks.

who: two hunters gutting a kill

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Open it from the vent. Don't nick the gut.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: I've dressed more deer than you've eaten.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Then why does it smell like that?

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Liver's mine. I took the shot.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: You took three shots. The liver's the cook's.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Save the blood. Black pudding's still food.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Save the hooves too. Nothing goes to waste this winter.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Hang it overnight. Flies are thick.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Hang it high. There's wolves about, and worse.

who: two guards or outlaw lookouts watching a road

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Dust on the road.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Carts or riders?

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Carts. Slow ones. Heavy ones.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Lord's seal on the lead cart.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Then it's ours. Fetch the others.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Nobody travels this road at night.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Somebody's carrying a lantern down there.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Then somebody's a fool, or bait.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: {band} hit the carts from {hamlet} last week.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: So we watch this bend. They like a bend.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Caravan from the oasis is late.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Late means taxed twice or robbed once.

who: two scholars or clerks in a library

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Who has the Riftlands roll?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Borrowed. Never returned.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: That's the third roll this month.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Candle's down to the stub.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Read faster. The librarian counts candles.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: This charter's half rot.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Then copy the half that isn't. It proves which hamlets are ours.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Someone's cut a page from the royal rolls.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Hush. Don't say that where the librarian can hear.

who: an innkeeper and a serving girl at a roadside inn

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Two more at the corner table. They want ale.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Do they want to pay for it?

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Ask after you pour.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Every bed's taken.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Put the rest in the stable and charge for the straw.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: They want meat.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Tell them it's pottage, and it's a fine pottage.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Merchant at the hearth says the road's not safe.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Merchants always say that. It's how they raise their prices.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Man in the hood won't give a name.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Then he pays first, and sleeps nearest the door.

who: two grooms mucking out a stable

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Whose turn is the warhorse?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Yours. He bit me last time.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: He bites everyone. It's how he says good morning.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Dung barrow's full already.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Tip it on the midden. The gardener will thank you.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Fine horse for a man in patched boots.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Not our business. Fork the straw.

who: two tower wardens cutting fuel for a beacon

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Pitch-pine for the core, green on top for smoke.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Who taught you that?

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: My father. His father taught him.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Haul it up before dusk.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Every dusk, every night. For what?

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: For the night we need it.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Cut double. I don't want to run short.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: You think the line will be called?

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: I think a calamity just rose.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Folk in town are cold and we burn wood on a hill.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Tell that to the next hamlet the Blight takes.

who: two labourers mending the ford's stones

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Stone's shifted again under the water.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Flood shifts it. Carts shift it more.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Hand me the crowbar.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Brother Roger says he'll bless the work.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: I'd rather he brought bread.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Who are we fixing this for, the band or the Company?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Whoever holds it when it's done.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Water's to my knees and colder than sin.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Then work faster and you'll be out sooner.

who: a healer and a helper over the wounded

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Hold him still.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: He's not moving much.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: That's why I need him held. The next part wakes them.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Boil the linens again.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Sister, they're clean.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: They're clean when the fever stays away.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: This wound's gone grey at the edges.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Blight?

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Cut it wide. And don't touch your eyes after.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Three more from {hamlet}.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Where do we put them?

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Wherever they'll fit. On the floor if we must.

who: two hired guards over a merchant's goods

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: What's in the crates?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Don't know, don't care. We're paid to care for it, not open it.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Someone was by the wagon.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: A dog?

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Dogs don't whistle, {B}.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Merchant wants us awake all night.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Merchant can pay us for all night, then.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Watch the boy by the {good}.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: He's a boy.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Boys have quick hands. Watch him.

who: two muleteers with their mules

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: This one's favouring the off fore.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Stone in the hoof. Hold her head.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Mules won't cross the stream.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Mules are cleverer than merchants. Find another way.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Feed them before they load, or they'll sulk all day.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: So will I if you don't feed me.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Water toll's up again at the spring.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Then the mules drink first, and us after.

who: two soldiers of the Grey Company storming the ford

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Shields up. They'll loose from the chapel wall.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Let them. They've arrows for one volley.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Then we wade.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Captain Young wants it by noon.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Captain Young will have it by noon.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Low-Water lot are dug in behind the carts.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Carts burn. Fetch the pitch.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Mind the friar. Roger's not to be harmed.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: He'll stand in the middle and pray at us.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Then go round him.

who: two fighters in the middle of a brawl or skirmish

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Behind you!

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: I see him!

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Then hit him!

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Not the benches! The innkeeper charges for benches!

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: He can bill the other fellow.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Close up! Don't let them get between us!

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: There's too many!

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: There's exactly enough. Swing.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Can't see who's who!

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: If he's swinging at you, he's theirs.

who: two scouts watching the ford from cover

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Six on the bank, one asleep.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: And the chapel?

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Friar's there. And someone on the roof.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: They've a fire on the near side.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Fools. Count the shapes round it.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Water's low today. You could ride across.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: So could they. Write it down.

who: two soldiers or militiamen arming

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Buckle my back strap.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Breathe in.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: I am breathing in. That's all there is.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Sergeant says full kit.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Full kit for what?

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: He didn't say. Which is why it's full kit.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: {band} took {hamlet}. We march at first light.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Then I'm sharpening this tonight.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: This mail's rusted through at the arm.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Then keep that arm out of the way.

who: two outlaws of the Low-Water band at the ford, or two Grey Company sellswords after

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Penny a head to cross.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: And if they won't pay?

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Then a penny a head's what we take off them.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Friar's at it again. Says the ford's God's.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Then God can pay us the toll.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Lord's hiring swords. Grey Company, they say.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Let them come. Water's deep in the middle.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Fog's on the water.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Fog's on our side. Nobody storms a ford they can't see.

who: Juliana the Warlock's apprentice and a water-seller at the last spring

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: The ward's humming louder today.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: That's her mending it.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Or someone pressing on it.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Toll's a coin a load.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: A coin! The oasis folk can't pay that.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Then the oasis folk can dig.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Do you see the light on the water?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: That's the ward. Don't put your hand in it.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Lantern mages were on the ridge again.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Juliana knows. Juliana always knows.

who: two mages over a scrying bowl

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Hold the bowl still.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: It is still. The water's moving on its own.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: I see the March. Fires.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Beacons?

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: No. Something burning that shouldn't burn.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: The water's gone black.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Then it's watching back. Cover it, quickly.

who: two free mages of the Company of the Lantern testing Juliana's ward

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Touch it there. Softly.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: It stung.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Good. Stinging means there's a seam.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: She's weaker after dark.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Or she wants us to think so.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Richard says one more week of this.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Richard says a lot of things. My fingers are numb.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Water belongs to everyone.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Tell that to the warlock with a ward round it.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: It moved. The whole weave moved toward us.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Back off. Now, {B}.

who: a scholar and an apprentice mage writing down the ward's pattern

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Seven strands, braided.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Eight. There's one beneath.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Then she's better than we were told.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Copy the knot exactly.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: My hand's shaking.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Then copy it twice.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: It glows brighter near midnight.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Mark the hour. Patterns have hours.

who: two mages of the Lantern breaking the ward on the last spring

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: All together, on my word.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: And if it bites back?

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Then it bites us all at once.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: It's cracking!

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Hold! Don't let go now!

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: There. Hear that?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: The water's running free.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Sunward will drink cheap tonight.

who: a librarian and a pupil

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: You've copied this word wrong.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: It's the same word.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Steward, not stewart. History lives in letters.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: What were the Stewards, sir?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Knights who kept the Rim. Now it means a man who counts grain.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Read me the Oath again.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: That copy is incomplete.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Why?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Someone wanted it that way. Read.

who: a clerk stamping a traveller's wanderbook, and the traveller

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Book.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Here.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Last stamp's from {town}? You walk a lot.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Two pennies for the seal.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: It was one penny last spring.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Last spring the roads were safer.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Is this your book or {player}'s?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Mine.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Then why does it smell of their pack?

who: two shepherds or wardens watching beasts hunt

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Pack's working the low meadow.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Driving the roe toward the stream.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Clever brutes. Cleverer than our dogs.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Hear them? Calling to each other.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Keep the fire high and the dogs tied.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Den's hungry, they say. Ranging further.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Then the folds are next.

who: two travellers or carters who see something following them

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Something's been keeping pace in the trees.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Deer.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Deer don't stop when you stop.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Walk faster.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Don't run. If it's a wolf, it likes running.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Eyes in the hedge.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Lantern up. Keep walking. Sing something.

who: two herb gatherers watching animals forage nearby

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Boar's been through the bracken.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Then the mushrooms are gone.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: And we leave before it comes back.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Bear's tearing at the old stump.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Grubs. Let her have them, and walk wide.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Even the beasts are hungry this year.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Beasts are honest about it, at least.

who: two shepherds as beasts attack their fold

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: They're at the fold! Get the torches!

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: I count five, maybe six!

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Shout, then! Shout loud!

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: They've taken the ram!

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Leave him! Close the hurdles!

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Third night this week.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: And the lodge sits on its bows.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Charter says they can't.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Charter's not a shepherd.

who: two tower wardens looking toward the Heart at night

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: The sky over the Heart's gone red.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: It's breathing.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Don't.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Feel that? In your teeth.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Like a bell, rung far away.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Like something drawing breath.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: {calamity} is risen.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: And the Heart's brighter for it.

who: two guild scouts watching the horde gather

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: They're forming up. Like soldiers.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Horrors don't form up.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: These do.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Count them.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: I stopped at three hundred.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Back to Blightwatch. Now.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Not running?

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Walking. Running draws the eye.

who: two outlaws in a camp near the March who see Blight-born testing the edge

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Something touched the stakes last night.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Wolf.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Wolves don't leave grey on the wood.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: It's walking the line of our fire.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Looking for the gap.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Then don't give it one.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: The Grey Crows lost four to these.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Then we move camp before it comes back with friends.

who: two guild adventurers watching a calamity's will take hold

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: The beasts have stopped fighting each other.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Something's holding them.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Something with a name we don't want to learn.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Every beast in the March turned to face east.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Toward {calamity}.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Toward its master.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: My head. There's a voice in my head.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Don't listen. Think of home. Think of anything.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: The jackals are walking in rows.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Then we're too close.

who: two survivors watching from cover as the Blight lays waste

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: That was a hamlet this morning.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: It was.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Smoke over {hamlet}.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: No smoke. Look again. It's grey dust rising.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: The fields are going grey as I look.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Don't look. Walk.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Did anyone get out?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Some. Not enough.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Pray for them later. Walk now.

who: two wardens or adventurers seeing a swarm of Blight-born

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: The ground's moving.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: That's not the ground.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Light the beacon! Light it!

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: It won't stop them.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: It'll stop the next town sleeping.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Up the rocks. They don't climb well.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Pray they don't learn.

who: two watchmen or shepherds who see a predator prowling

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Big cat on the ridge.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Or a big shadow.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Shadows don't twitch their tails.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Something's round the back of the barn.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Bear?

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Too quiet for a bear.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Footprints in the furrows.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Wolf. A big one, alone.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Alone ones are the hungry ones.

who: two foresters or shepherds watching deer browse

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Hind and two calves at the edge of the copse.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Lord's deer.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Lord's deer eating the lord's hazel.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: They come out at first light.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: So do the poachers.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Look how they lift their heads together.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: They've heard us. Stand still.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: They've stripped the young oaks again.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Sawyers will curse the deer and the deer won't care.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: That's a winter of meat standing there.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: That's a rope for your neck standing there.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Count them for the lodge.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Nine. Half's four and a half.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Then the lodge takes four and argues about the half.

who: two herdsmen watching livestock or wild goats graze

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Flock's settled.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Then sit. You've earned it.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Move them up the hill after noon.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Grass is thin up there.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Wolves are thick down here.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Goats on the Wall again.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Goats always find the worst ledge.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Gazelle on the far dune.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Lord lost one last hunt. Court still laughs.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Fat ewes this year.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Fat ewes, fat lambs, fat wolves. It all comes round.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Don't let them near the barley.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: They can smell it from here.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: So can I.

who: two farm hands watching beasts feed

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Pigs ate the whole trough.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Pigs always eat the whole trough. That's what pigs are for.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Rooks on the seed.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Throw stones. Not at me, {B}.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Ducks are in from the fen.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Fowlers will be glad.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Animals eat better than us this month.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Then eat an animal.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Steward counts them.

who: two night watchmen or shepherds hearing beasts feed in the dark

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Hear that crunching?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Something's at the turnips.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Better turnips than us.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Badgers in the oats.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Badgers or boar?

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Boar. Badgers don't grunt like that.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Lantern shows eyes along the hedge.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Deer. Throw a clod.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Throw it yourself.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Pack got into a camp's stores, they say.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Ours are locked. Mostly.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Otters at the fish weir again.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: They've better fishing rights than we do.

who: two foresters hearing stags in rut

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Listen. Roaring in the glen.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: The stags are at it.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Lord will want a hunt now.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Two of them, antlers locked.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Leave them. They'll kill each other for us.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Don't go near a rutting stag.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: He's half a mile off.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Half a mile's nothing to a stag that thinks you're a rival.

who: two farmers or foresters watching boar root

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Sounder's in the beechmast.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Six, and a big sow.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Big sow means stay up the bank.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Ground's turned like a plough's been through.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Boar. Fresh.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: The old boar's out again.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: The one with the torn ear?

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: He's outlived three huntsmen. Leave him.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Lord's hunt brought one to bay last week.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Feast for days. Pray they bring another.

who: two farmers finding boar in their crops

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: They're in the turnips!

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Get the dogs! Get the sticks!

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Whole row's gone.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Lord won't let us kill them.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Lord's not eating turnips this winter.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: That's half our winter dug up.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Then we eat the boar, and say a wolf took it.

who: two lodge hunters scouting a beast den

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Bones at the mouth. Fresh.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: How many?

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: More than we'd want.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Wind's toward us. Good.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Good for us. Bad for whatever's inside.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Den's hungry. They'll range tonight.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Then we tell the folds before dark.

who: two adventurers searching a ruin for a relic

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Academy says it's under the altar.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Academy also said five of them came back.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: One did.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Something moved in the crypt.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Rats.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Rats don't breathe that loud.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Dig there. Stones are newer.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Someone's been here before us.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Then they found it, or it found them.

who: two of the lord's huntsmen with a lymer hound on the leash

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: She's got a line.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Fresh?

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Look at her tail. Fresh as morning.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Keep her quiet. A lymer doesn't bay.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: She knows. Better than you do.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Slots in the mud. A hart of ten, I'd say.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Break a twig to mark it. {lord} will want the great one.

who: two of the lord's huntsmen rousing the quarry

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Beat the covert from the east.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: And if he breaks west?

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Then the relay hounds are there.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: There he goes!

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Sound the horn. Let {lord} hear it.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Steady. Make noise, not haste.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Noise I can do.

who: two huntsmen riding in the lord's chase

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Hounds are running!

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Keep up! The lord won't wait!

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Ditch ahead!

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Jump it or lose the hunt!

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Where's {lord}?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Out front, where he wants to be seen.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Last hunt the lodge took three beasts.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: This hunt we'll take the one that matters.

who: two huntsmen after the hounds lose the line

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: They've checked.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Lost it at the stream.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Cast them downstream. He'll have walked the water.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: {lord} will be in a mood.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: {lord} is always in a mood. Find the line.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Lost the gazelle again.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Court will be laughing a month.

who: two huntsmen as the quarry is brought to bay

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: He's at bay! Hold the hounds!

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Leave him for {lord}. Don't you dare loose.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Boar's backed against the rock.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Spears low. He'll come for the hounds first.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Hart's turned in the water.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Mind the antlers. They gore the brave ones.

who: two guild scouts witnessing the Blight unmake the land

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: The trees are going to dust.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Not dust. Nothing.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: The stones are crying out.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Don't listen. Keep your hood up and walk.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: {calamity} is doing this.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Or Drakrevor. Does it matter which?

who: two huntsmen carrying venison from the hunt

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Haunch is heavier than the stag was.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: That's the honour of it.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Keep it covered. Flies, and eyes.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Whose eyes?

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Hungry ones. Lean year.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: The kitchens will want this tonight.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Then walk faster, and stop grumbling.

who: a huntsman and a cook or steward receiving venison

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Hindquarter for the high table.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: And the rest?

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Umbles for the huntsmen. That's the custom.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: {steward} will count it.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Then count it with him. I'll not be called a thief.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: There's folk in town who'd kill for this.

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: There's a lord upstairs who'd kill for it too.

who: two shepherds or watchmen fighting off beasts at a fold

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Fire! Wave the fire!

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: They're not afraid of it!

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Then hit them with it!

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Over the hurdles!

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Watch the gap! Watch the gap!

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Not again! Not tonight!

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Then fight like it's the last time!

who: two guards rushing the walls

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Everyone up! On the walls!

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Who's coming?

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: More than enough! Move!

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Torches along the parapet!

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Archers to the gate!

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: {band} are coming from {hamlet}!

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Shut the gate! Shut it!

who: two townsfolk ringing the alarm bell

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Ring it! Ring it hard!

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: My arms!

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Your arms or your neck!

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Wake them all!

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: They're waking! Lights in the windows!

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Ring the big bell, not the mass bell!

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Which rope is which?

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: The thick one!

who: two villagers raising the hue and cry

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Thief! Stop thief!

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Which way?

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Toward the road! Out! Everyone out!

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Out! Out! The hue is raised!

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Every man to the chase!

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Robbery! Robbery on the road!

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Light torches! Wake the sergeant!

who: two people woken by an alarm

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Up! Up!

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: What is it?

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Bell's ringing! Up!

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Fire or raid?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Doesn't matter! Get your boots on!

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Children! Get the children!

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: I've got them! Go!

who: two tower wardens lighting the beacon

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Light it! Light it now!

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: It's wet!

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Pitch, then! Burn the pitch!

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Is the next one lit?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Not yet! Not yet!

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Keep yours bright! They'll see it!

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: The March beacons are dark!

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Then ours is the first warning! Burn!

who: a victim and a watchman reporting a robbery

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Robbed! On the road!

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Slow down. How many were they?

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Four. Five. They took everything!

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Did they give a name?

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: The leader called himself {band}.

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: My cart, my mules, all of it!

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Not the first today. Sit down.

who: two guards patrolling the road

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Keep up! The carts are waiting!

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: We're behind!

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Then run! The road's not safe!

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: Movement in the ditch!

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Swords out! Call out!

lines.speaker: A
lines.text: They hit the last carts!

lines.speaker: B
lines.text: Then we're too late! Move!
